$comment: meme-registry/1 — the Muha Meds meme knowledge graph. Everything an agent needs to recreate a sent meme or build a new one around a Muha device: which device body (and its verbatim prompt block), which meme GRAMMAR the joke uses, which PIPELINE + PROVIDER will actually accept the source material, where templates can be sourced with provenance, every meme shipped so far with its card geometry, and the law bank measured across those builds. Paths are repo-relative; `Muha Memes/` is LOCAL-ONLY (ignored by the curated .gitignore), so template/asset paths resolve on the build machine, not on a fresh clone. Retrieval: `npm run content -- knowledge query "muha meme <grammar|template|device>" --brand muha`. Operator doc: docs/IMAGE_KNOWLEDGE_GRAPH.md (Meme registry section) + Muha Memes/HANDOFF__MUHA_MEMES.md.
workflow: 1. Classify the source: still or video; which IP class (see sourcing.ipClasses); which grammar (grammars[]) the joke runs on; which device body the brief names (devices[]).

2. Measure the card before anything else — canvas, caption ink, image band, watermark — and record it in the template entry. Cards differ every time (white 16:9 band, black 2.39:1 band, square band, multi-panel stills).

3. Pick the pipeline by source class + grammar (pipelines[] `when`), and the provider from providers[] — never conclude a route is blocked without running a control (law meme:control-before-concluding).
4. Pass the device by REFERENCE (registry devices[].refs) plus its verbatim deviceBlock. Never describe a device from memory; never composite/PIL-paste it into the frame.
5. Generate 3-4 candidates per hypothesis; diff them against the template to catch reframes; check every hand grips, every badge fits its face, and no type was invented.
6. Captions, labels, watermarks and legal lines are composed deterministically AFTER generation (card.py / memecard.sh / buildcard.py) — exact strings, never model-drawn.
7. Record the shipped file under templates[].outputs, add new rejections as laws, and keep the SKU shown to a real one (devices[].skus).

grammars.name: Swap what a hand holds
grammars.mechanism: The subject already holds something (cigarette, martini, pitchfork, boombox, earring, phone); the device takes its place in the same grip.
grammars.strength: strongest and cheapest — same placement, nothing to fade in
requires: grip clause (fingers close around it, thumb across; hand and object read as one shape)
size anchored to the hand, not the frame

grammars.name: Swap what the subject wears
grammars.mechanism: A hat/cap becomes the Muha captain hat (or a device-crested item). Same shape, same placement.
grammars.strength: very reliable in v2v — nothing to fade in
requires: say it is on in the very first frame
deviceFit: brand marks, not the device itself

grammars.name: The device as architecture
grammars.mechanism: A tower, post, pole or monolith in the scene becomes the device.
grammars.strength: atmospheric; the joke reads at card scale
requires: terse body + strong distance/mist language or the plate turns into a product render
monochrome tone map stated explicitly on b/w plates

grammars.name: Devices AS the characters
grammars.mechanism: The scene is re-staged with devices standing in for the actors (Titanic bow).
grammars.strength: regenerated scene — zero footage IP, but the least faithful to the original
requires: blocking diagram instead of the real frame (moderation)
short stubby cartoon arms, thickness/length caps

grammars.name: Many identical devices around the subject
Two hands / two characters bringing halves together
grammars.mechanism: The famous gap (fingertips, two friends) closes on the magnetic pair.
requires: measure hand and device sizes; correct with numbers

grammars.name: Held overhead / large in frame
grammars.mechanism: A big prop (boombox) becomes the product, large enough for badges to read.
grammars.strength: the only grammar where badge lettering reliably resolves

grammars.name: Object resting in a lap or on a table
grammars.mechanism: The device sits with the subject (Mona Lisa's lap, the cat's table).
requires: two passes: place, then close the hand

grammars.name: Replace the small floating subject
grammars.mechanism: The butterfly, the pills, the balloon become the device.
requires: state position and size as 'exactly where X was'

grammars.name: The device at planet/monument scale
grammars.mechanism: Earth, a moon, a mountain becomes a giant device.
requires: 'in exactly the place and at exactly the size of X'

grammars.name: Two hands on one device
grammars.mechanism: A handshake/arm-wrestle becomes a shared grip — two flavours, one device.
requires: device small, gold cap clear of the fingers

grammars.name: Draw a continuation panel in the template's style
grammars.mechanism: The template's last panel is answered by a new one (the sweating man now relaxed with the device).
grammars.strength: lets a text-only template carry the product

grammars.name: Reaction image under a lowercase caption bar
grammars.mechanism: A relatable first-person caption ('me when…', 'friend: / me:', 'pov:') sits in a white bar above a reaction image — an animal, a puppet, a cartoon, or a phone-photo mood — in which the device is simply present. The caption carries the joke; the product is never named.
grammars.strength: the Gen Z brand-page native format; the operator's answer to 'corny'
requires: lowercase sentence case, Helvetica Neue Medium, no caps, no product copy
phone-photo realism for generated scenes (auto-exposure, grain, clutter)
device small and incidental, never consumed

pipelines.name: Regenerate the scene (video)
pipelines.when: The joke can be re-staged with devices as characters; source footage only a reference.
steps: device-only crop refs
flat grey BLOCKING DIAGRAM of the composition (never the real film frame)
Nano Banana Pro start frame 16:9 2K with device refs + diagram
Veo 3.1 i2v (--quality high --variant veo-3-1-preview, 4/6/8s) with an absolute camera lock
memecard.sh rebuilds the measured card

pipelines.name: Edit the real footage (video)
pipelines.when: The original footage must be preserved (actors, famous shot).
steps: measure the card; crop the video band; upscale
retime UP to the next whole second (MiniMax bills integers, caps at 15s)
minimax_h3 with --video-references + --image-references (object ref) and a SHORT source-anchored prompt
splice.py: resample back to the source frame count, per-channel tone match, write only into the band, restore watermark/caption pixels, mux original audio (-c:a copy)
frames piped straight to ffmpeg, never staged as PNGs
pipelines.cost: minimax_h3 5s=20 / 10s=40 / 15s=60 credits; 4 concurrent jobs shared across sessions

pipelines.name: Still meme edit with gpt-image-2
pipelines.when: Default for stills: cartoons, photos, paintings without nudity.
steps: template = REFERENCE 1 (layout master), device Front + 45 renders as REFERENCE 2/3
prompt: KEEP (edge to edge, no zoom/crop/redraw) + THE ONE CHANGE + GRIP + SMALL + verbatim device block + 'no text'
/v1/images/edits, size = template aspect rounded to /16 (ladder steps down on size errors), quality medium (high needs a 300s timeout), 3-4 candidates, FormData rebuilt per attempt
diff every candidate vs the template (mean-abs-diff, % pixels >25) — a reframe is a bright everywhere-diff
captions/labels composed with card.py

pipelines.name: Still meme edit with Nano Banana Pro
pipelines.when: gpt-image-2 refuses the frame (classical nudes) or the hands must be repainted to grip in a painterly style.
steps: gemini-3-pro-image-preview, parts = [template, device refs, prompt], imageConfig aspectRatio + 2K
then targeted fix passes: feed the approved frame back, name every finished element as off-limits, change ONE thing, give MEASUREMENTS not adjectives, re-measure after

pipelines.name: Per-panel inpaint with Seedream v5 Pro (Higgsfield)
pipelines.when: A multi-panel still where each panel is edited separately and must stay in register; accepts real actors' likenesses.
steps: crop + upscale each panel
seedream_v5_pro is_inpaint true at the panel's exact aspect (custom --width/--height; enum aspects reframe), refs = plate then device
buildcard.py: resample back, per-channel tone match per panel, restore original watermark glyphs

pipelines.name: Captions and cards are drawn, never generated
steps: measure the card geometry per clip/still
card.py (Impact / Arial / white-band styles, fractional coordinates) or memecard.sh / buildcard.py
restore watermarks and captions from original pixels through a luminance mask

pipelines.name: Fix one element on an approved frame
pipelines.when: One hand/badge/size is wrong and the rest is signed off.
steps: approved frame back in as the base
list every finished element by name as off-limits
state the one change with a MEASUREMENT (pixels + %, or margins as one geometry)
3-4 candidates; measure; expect a fix to break something adjacent and re-check the whole frame

sourcing.policy: Sent memes are the primary source (the operator forwards clips/stills with a caption already written). For self-sourced templates, record provenance + IP class per file and prefer the lowest-exposure class that carries the joke. Children never; real private individuals only when the template is a universally licensed meme; celebrities carry moderation AND likeness exposure — run them as N=1 tests and let the client decide.

routes.how: GET https://api.imgflip.com/get_memes -> 100 most-used templates with id, name, WxH, box_count and a direct https://i.imgflip.com/<id>.<ext> URL. No auth. Download with a browser UA.

https://imgflip.com/memesearch?q=<terms> lists /meme/<id>/<slug> links; the template page https://imgflip.com/memetemplate/<id>/<slug> contains the i.imgflip.com image URL. Used for 'Both is good', 'Why not both', Morpheus pills, Two Wolves, Trolley Problem, Choose Your Fighter, Kronk/Homer angel-devil.

GET https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&titles=File:<name>&prop=imageinfo&iiprop=url|size|extmetadata&iiurlwidth=1920&format=json with a descriptive User-Agent (a guessed upload.wikimedia.org thumb path returns 400). extmetadata.LicenseShortName carries the licence; 'Public domain' paintings = zero IP exposure. American Gothic (1930) entered the US public domain 2026-01-01.

laws.claim: A `failed` job returns no reason. Run a control first (same model, same prompt shape, a non-copyrighted image). Control passes => the footage is the trigger => try another provider. Never conclude 'every route refuses this' from routes that share a provider.
laws.evidence: Captain Phillips 2026-08-18: three shared-provider failures were wrongly read as universal, pushing a composite the operator rejected; MiniMax H3 then did it first pass.

laws.claim: The meme frame goes in as REFERENCE 1 and the prompt says it is reproduced edge to edge at the same framing, with nothing enlarged, moved or run off an edge; the device renders are references so the product is reproduced rather than invented.
laws.evidence: SpongeBob first pass cut Patrick's head off before the edge-to-edge clause; every magnetic meme since holds framing.

laws.claim: Say the hand GRIPS: fingers wrapping the body, thumb across, hand and object one solid shape. Without it the device hovers in mid-air beside an open hand.
laws.evidence: SpongeBob, Creation (left index finger stayed extended until named), Mona Lisa (floating device until the second pass).

laws.claim: Anchor an inserted object's size to a body part ('as long as his palm, no wider than two fingers', 'roughly a small lighter in an adult grip', 'a third the height of the face'), never to the frame, and say 'if in doubt make it smaller'. Frame fractions set scale but not proportion; an object with nothing to sit against gets oversized.
laws.evidence: Yacht party device larger than a head; yacht s06 console placement oversized vs held; Creation devices dwarfing hands until sized against the hand.

laws.claim: Give a MEASUREMENT and a target, not an adjective. 'Smaller' was ignored twice; '190px vs 105px, redraw at 55%' and 'about 105 pixels wide, centred, ~16px bare black either side' landed in one pass. Always measure after a size pass — four plausible candidates can all be unchanged.
laws.evidence: Creation left hand; Cannes badge; Mona Lisa 60% pass (429px before and after).

laws.claim: Stack two changes and the model satisfies the easier one. Size alone halved the Mona Lisa device immediately after 'size AND clean badges' changed only the badges.

A correction pass rerolls everything not named as off-limits. Feed the approved frame back in, list every finished element (the other hand, the other device, the framing, the field, the face) and change one thing; then re-check the whole frame because a fix breaks something adjacent.
laws.evidence: fix-lefthand (grip fix inflated the hand), fix-jh, fix-badge-pos.

laws.claim: Badge lettering resolves as a function of the device's pixel footprint, not prompt wording: ~140x259px device smears no matter what (8 passes), ~160x300 holds; wordy badges belong on memes that hold the product large (boombox), fruit-shaped badges read small (Ibiza Cherry, Purple Punch). Pushing harder for type makes the model ENLARGE the badge instead.
laws.evidence: Mona Lisa badge passes; boombox vs Creation comparison.

laws.claim: Nano Banana Pro will not rescale a badge on a rendered device (16 candidates, every phrasing, incl. a pixel target and an exemplar); it rescales whole devices fine. gpt-image-2 /v1/images/edits does it when given width in pixels + equal margins as ONE geometry.

Asking gpt-image-2 to MOVE a badge makes it enlarge it and the fault swaps sides; ask for a FIT (width + equal margins) and you get both. Check whether the badge fits the flat face before promising to move it.
laws.evidence: 'slide it right' c1-c3 all grew 4-30px and ran off the opposite edge.

laws.claim: Read the device's flat face off a luminance profile across the badge row, not by eye: shoulder = dark fall-off then a bright specular band, flat face = the long even stretch. Foreshortening makes the two halves very different; measure each.
laws.evidence: Misread the shoulder side twice; boombox gold face was 98px not 140.

laws.claim: Diff every candidate against the approved frame (mean-abs-diff + % pixels differing by >25). A good edit is one bright blob on the changed element; a reframe lights up everywhere (10.7/10.5% vs 3.6/1.2%). Check faces numerically (crop + mean-abs-diff) to catch a stylised repaint.
laws.evidence: cannesgpt c1 reframed; bbclean face diff 4.6 = re-encode noise only.

laws.claim: gpt-image-2 rejects about one candidate in four at random on identical prompts ('rejected by the safety system'). Over-request and let one fail; do not reword and do not read a block as 'refuses this frame'. A whole-batch refusal on a nude is real (Creation) — switch to Nano Banana.
laws.evidence: Cannes/London fix runs at all three sizes; Creation 3/3 refused.

laws.claim: Every correction pass through Nano Banana at 2K leaves a painterly smear, a purple cast and a distorted face that compounds; base every edit on the untouched original the client supplied and refit elements with gpt-image-2 (which preserved the photograph: face diff 4.6).
laws.evidence: boombox_edge/str chain vs boombox-original-clean + fix-boombox-clean c3.

laws.claim: A meme must show a real SKU. Pairings are fixed by the product (magnetic: black half + gold half table; dual flavor: left name + right name table). A pass that picked badges freely produced two non-existent products.
laws.evidence: MagneticDispo README 'THE COMBOS ARE FIXED SKUs'; Dual Flavor pairs read off the screens 2026-09-10.

laws.claim: Ban text by category ('no wordmark, no lettering, no words, no numbers, no small print'); never write the brand string inside a negative — the model renders it. Small type on a device is allowed to be soft; readable words must never be invented. Captions, labels, watermarks are composed deterministically afterwards.

State BLACK AND GOLD as a hard product fact in one paragraph, then subordinate it to the plate's light in a second ('lit by this scene, not a studio, no hard white hotspot'), then name the panel's own light on the gold. Merging them yields either a silhouette or a hero render.
laws.evidence: Pole s3 (glossy gold product render) vs g1-g3 pick; 'shadowed' round rejected as all-black.

laws.claim: For multiples: (1) IDENTICAL COPIES — every instance the exact same product differing only in angle/distance, no design change during the shot; (2) a COUNT; (3) DEPTH routing — never between camera and subject, pass BEHIND the silhouette. Without (1) instances diverge; without (2) shots come back empty; forbidding a position leaves it ambiguous.
laws.evidence: BrainCompute P_head_tiny_v3.txt; also holds multi-panel stills together (Pole).

laws.claim: v2v prompts must be SHORT and source-anchored ('keep this shot exactly, change only X'). A 2500-char canonical description flipped MiniMax from editing to generating: it changed the vessel and re-framed nine of twelve shots.

In v2v the REFERENCE IMAGE drives framing, not the prompt: a rich master render pushes the camera in to honour its detail; a plain device crop holds the source framing. Swap the ref before adding 'do not zoom' language. The ref's own aspect also drives the rendered proportion (a 1:1.5 crop => stubby device).
laws.evidence: Escobar v4 vs v6 (same prompt); yacht s06 pen_capcrest vs device-rich.

laws.claim: Asking for a legible mark on a distant subject makes the model push in. Say the mark may be small, soft or illegible at this distance and that is correct; size creeps up whenever markings are requested — blank bodies hold size.
laws.evidence: Yacht hull mark; yacht s06 marked vs blank takes.

laws.claim: State that an added/swapped object is present in the very first frame and never appears or fades in, or v2v introduces it ~2s late. Swapping something the subject already wears/holds beats adding.
laws.evidence: Captain Phillips, YachtMaster, Wan 2.6 late hat.

laws.claim: MiniMax H3 bills integer seconds, caps at 15, returns its own resolution @24fps. Retime the source UP to the next whole second (keeps every frame), resample back to the source frame count, tone-match per channel, restore original caption/watermark pixels, mux the original audio. Extract the frame range THEN setpts, never in one chain.

A real film frame as a composition ref fails Nano Banana Pro moderation on the actors' likenesses; a flat grey blocking diagram (capsules, arms, horizon, rigging) called out as 'layout only' works with zero IP.

On a black-and-white plate say what each material renders AS ('the cap renders NEAR-WHITE, the brightest thing in frame') — 'polished gold' means nothing in monochrome and rendered black twice. 'Lit from within' beats 'glowing'; 'do NOT brighten / clean up / smooth the grain' is load-bearing.

Keep the device description SHORT on atmospheric/distant plates; the long flavour block pulled the lighthouse out of the fog into a clean product render. Blank body + strong distance/mist language holds it back.

Measure the card before anything else and never reuse the last card's numbers: white 16:9 band (Titanic 1080x1920 / Escobar 480x854), black 2.39:1 band with subtitles (Captain Phillips), square band (YachtMaster => --aspect-ratio 1:1, no letterboxing), 3-panel 2.4:1 (Pole), 2-panel with a b/w right half (Lighthouse).

Compositing a device/badge into a meme is rejected: it sits ON hands rather than in them, flat pastes cannot match painted lighting/perspective, and clearing the old artefact samples the wrong surface. Generate with the real asset as a reference; keep composites only as documented fallbacks.
laws.evidence: Creation composite rejected by the client; boombox 'fixed' composite killed the gloss; feedback_never_composite_generate_whole_graphic.

laws.claim: Higgsfield allows 4 concurrent jobs per ACCOUNT (shared across sessions; excess submissions vanish with rate_limit_reached) — batch 3 and verify every job returned a URL. Never stage PNG frames on this machine; pipe frames to ffmpeg.

The Dual Flavor device is a stout 2.1:1 pill with fully rounded ends and twin mouthpieces; earlier Muha memes taught the models a slim 3.3:1 slab, so the pill proportions, the two mouthpieces and 'not a pen' must be in the block or the older body comes back.

laws.claim: gpt-image-2 will draw a NEW panel that continues a comic template in its own style (same character, line weight and palette) when the template is passed only as a style reference — Two Buttons relief panel 3/3 usable. Compose the strip and its labels deterministically afterwards (compose_two_buttons.py finds the buttons by their red pixels).

Calibrate the candidate-vs-template diff per template before judging: a clean edit on a cartoon/photo reads 2.5-8 mean-abs-diff, a public-domain painting re-rendered at a new size reads 11-15 with NO reframe, and a real reframe reads 37-90 (both-is-good NB c1 84% px, woman-cat c1/c2 45-58%). The number ranks candidates within one template; it does not compare templates. Always look.

Nano Banana Pro is a fallback only when the frame can tolerate a re-render: on Both Is Good it re-laid the burned-in lettering into two lines, re-framed the scene and (in one candidate) redrew the device as the slim slab; adding an absolute framing lock did not help and tripped PROHIBITED_CONTENT. gpt-image-2 edits keep the frame; NB regenerates it.

Deterministic captions still need a layout pass: a title box that wraps to two lines walks into the subtitle (Buff Doge took three iterations — size the title to ONE line, then place the subtitle). Coordinates in fractions of the image keep one spec valid across candidate sizes.

For the Dual Flavor the operator picks classic caption-format templates where a CHARACTER HOLDS the device as the punchline (Two Buttons relief panel, Drake, 'is this a switch?'); public-domain art memes, no-face photo templates and device-as-scenery grammars were all rejected in the same review. All memes ship 4:5 portrait.
laws.evidence: Operator review 2026-09-10: liked two-buttons, pigeon, drake; disliked the other nine; 'all memes should 4:5 portrait'.
laws.counterexamples: The magnetic-pair art memes (Creation of Adam, Mona Lisa) were approved in September — the art grammar works for the two-halves joke, not for the dual-flavour choice joke.

laws.claim: 4:5 portrait is built after generation, not requested from the model: pad with the template's own flat background (white for wojak/comic drawings, black for dark plates), crop when the content allows (Drake: narrow the white text half), lay multi-panel strips into a 4:5 grid (Two Buttons 2-up + relief panel), and only outpaint full-bleed scenes with gpt-image-2 from a letterboxed grey canvas. Captions use fractions of the FINAL canvas so one spec fits every candidate.

gpt-image-2 will extend a finished meme to 4:5 from a letterboxed canvas: paste the picture on a 4:5 canvas with flat mid-grey bands, say the bands are to be painted as a continuation and the middle comes back unchanged. Both candidates on the anime frame came back seamless (window continued above, bush and sign below) with the device where it was. It re-renders the frame slightly cleaner than a VHS-soft original — acceptable for cartoons, check faces on photos.

A MOVE instruction lands when it carries the current centre, the target centre, the target bottom edge and the unchanged pixel height ('~470px tall, centre x=1356,y=390 → x=1130,y=640, bottom ≈ y=875'); two of three candidates moved the device to the hand at the same size and cleaned the old spot, the third ignored it. Without numbers a move becomes a resize (law meme:move-becomes-resize).

The LightOnOff renders (magenta LED = left flavour, green = right) let one meme show the switch mechanic with two copies of the SAME device — Morpheus's palms held one of each, glow on the skin, 3/3 first pass. Pass the two LED renders as separate references and state they are the same product differing only in LED colour.

Product-forward captions in Impact caps read as corny to the operator ('think about memes a company meme page would post… relatable to gen z'). The working voice is a lowercase, deadpan first-person caption bar that never names the product, the tagline, the mg or the mechanic; the device just sits in the frame. Templates from 2012 (Expanding Brain, Bell Curve, Roll Safe, Harold) age the post; reaction animals and phone-photo moods do not.
laws.evidence: Round-2 verdict 2026-09-10; round-3 built in the new voice (final_genz/).
laws.counterexamples: The operator still liked Two Buttons, Drake and 'is this a switch?' — classic templates work when the caption is a joke, not copy.

laws.claim: gpt-image-2 generates convincing phone-photo reaction images with the device from the Front+45 refs alone (no template): deadpan cat at a table, capybara, hamster, retriever balancing it on its nose, a hand with the green LED at night, a 2am nightstand — 17/18 candidates rendered, every device geometry held, and the phone-photo realism clauses (auto-exposure, grain, clutter, 'not a product shot') kept them off the AI-glossy look.

Animals never hold the device in the mouth or 'use' it: balance it on the head or nose, stand it beside them, or leave it on the table. Brand rule (no consumption depicted) plus optics — an animal with a vape in its mouth is the edgy read the operator ruled out.
laws.evidence: Design choice on dog-nose (treat-on-nose trick) 2026-09-10; sieve brand.json category_risk.

laws.claim: On the caption-bar card a wide template leaves a tall white bar the operator reads as dead space ('less white and dead space'). Crop the frame to 1:1 around the subject + device (Squidward: x 0.09→1.0 of the 1.43 frame) so the image fills ~80% of the card and the bar is ~270px. Tall bars only for genuinely wide two-panel templates (monkey puppet) where cropping would cut a panel.

In phone-photo 'mood' scenes (nightstand, party counter) the incidental device must still be noticed: aim for ~15-20% of frame height with the screen lit so the gauge and names glow. The first nightstand pass at ~105px wide in 1088 was 'not noticeable'; a measured 1.5x + lit-screen pass fixed it 3/3.

Generated reaction animals that render first pass with the device and read as Gen Z meme-page material: deadpan cat at a table, black cat peeking over a table edge, guilty pug, goose staring down, chameleon, meerkat row, husky mid-howl, shocked barn owl, two cats facing away, sloth, beagle in reading glasses, cat pushing the device off a counter, capybara, hamster, retriever balancing it on its nose. 36/36 and 17/18 across two rounds; no moderation refusals on animals.

An 'enlarge' pass on a lying-down device tends to grow its LENGTH more than its width (the body below the LED stretched to ~1.8x the true proportion). Follow any enlarge with a proportion check against the Front render, and if it drifted, run a shorten pass that fixes the width in pixels and moves the LED window back near the bottom end — that landed 3/3.

The Lion King 'presentation' composition with a vape is refused on every still route: gpt-image-2 0/3 and Nano Banana 0/2 on the Disney frame, Seedream failed, AND Nano Banana 0/2 on an original-design mandrill re-stage with no Disney frame at all — so the block is not only the IP; a cartoon character ceremonially presenting a vape trips it too. Do not spend more still candidates; the remaining routes are MiniMax H3 v2v on the real GIF or an untouched GIF with a caption bar.
laws.counterexamples: gpt-image-2 re-stage result pending in the same session (see template entry).

laws.claim: Veo 3.1 (Higgsfield CLI) returned status 'nsfw' on an image-to-video from a cartoon frame of a character holding the vape aloft — a video-side moderation distinct from the still refusals. The still itself passed gpt-image-2 (1/2) once the Disney frame was dropped and the character was an original design.
laws.counterexamples: Veo 3.1 animated the Titanic device start frames (2026-08-18) — devices as characters, no one 'presenting' one.
laws.confidence: provisional — one job; retry via the Higgsfield MCP and alternate models

laws.claim: For a cartoon character presenting the vape, Veo 3.1 and Seedance 2.0 both returned 'nsfw' on the same start frame while Kling 3.0 pro rendered it cleanly (5s, 1080p, device held every frame). Route 'character + vape' i2v to Kling first; keep Veo for device-as-character scenes. MiniMax H3 i2v cannot take image_references alongside start_image.
laws.counterexamples: Kling's camera discipline was poor on the Titanic bow (2026-08-18); on this static presentation shot it held.

laws.claim: Small screen type on the device (the puff counters) is re-synthesised every frame by i2v models and drifts ('00 00' → '30 399'). The lever that worked was NOT resolution (the 4K take still drifted) but MOTION: a prompt that freezes the character's hands and the device ('do not move, tilt or drift; the screen stays exactly as in the first frame') and moves only wind, light, distant animals and a slow push-in kept the counters stable. The type stays soft — that is the ceiling; if the digits must be crisp, composite the clean first-frame screen back over a static device.
laws.evidence: Muha Memes/DualFlavor/review/_lk_compare.jpg — original vs frozen vs 4K takes, 2026-09-11.

laws.claim: When the operator wants a GIF to look like the original, the order is: (1) MiniMax H3 v2v on the real loop (an animated PNG counts — build a 5s mp4 by repeating the frames; pass the device as image_references, NEVER with start_image; include the hand-anchored SIZE rule or the device comes back bigger than the head); (2) a blocking diagram measured off the frame + a precise design description on gpt-image-2 (2/3 passed where the Disney frame as reference was 0/3); (3) only then a free re-stage, which drifts in pose and design. The source's own actions survive v2v (the exhale puff), so check compliance frame by frame.

On a raised, open hand MiniMax v2v enlarges BOTH the inserted device and the hand to fit it (Tin Man take 1). Saying the hand stays its original size, giving the device as a fraction of the subject's height in pixels, and passing the plainer 45° render brought the hand back and halved the device; it still landed about head-sized, so expect two takes and start from the strict form.

A leftover from the swapped prop (the empty raised hand that held the hose) can be removed with a second MiniMax v2v pass that takes the FIRST pass's output as the video reference, no image ref, one short sentence. It held the device and rings; each pass eases the framing a little, so chain at most two. The account's 4-job cap is shared with other sessions — submit inside a retry loop (rate_limit → sleep 60).

MiniMax H3 is not universally safe on live-action: the Iron Man hologram clip (recognisable actor, close-up face) returned 'nsfw' twice, with and without the word 'vape', on the same day the Tin Man clip (costumed actor, face small) passed 2/2. Treat a real, recognisable face close to the inserted device as a refusal risk; run the coin control before spending more takes.
laws.evidence: Muha Memes/DualFlavor/hf/tonystark_minimax*.txt vs tinman_minimax*.txt, 2026-09-11. Coin control (no device, no ref) also 'nsfw' 2026-09-11 — the footage is the trigger.
laws.counterexamples: Captain Phillips / YachtMaster / Escobar all passed MiniMax in August with a hat or a plain device — the device was small and the object was not a vape in the prompt.

laws.claim: MiniMax H3 v2v will not set the SIZE of an inserted held object from words — 'same length as the bone', 'half', 'twice as long as wide' and a pixel rule all missed. It does copy size from a SIZE STILL: composite the product render at the wanted length into one source frame (PIL), clean it with a gpt-image-2 edit (remove the old prop's remainder, lips/hand wrap the object), then pass that still as the image reference with the untouched source video. Adding the product render as a second image reference roughly doubles the rendered size versus the still alone; a 'shrink it' pass on an already-swapped clip does not shrink the object, it zooms the whole scene out and invents set. MiniMax fills the source's pillarbox bars progressively, so crop deliveries to the FIRST frame's bars, not cropdetect's minimum.
laws.evidence: Dog-bone clip 2026-09-11: takes 7–10 (words) bracketed short/long/longer/longer; take 11 (size still at 0.30 head) → ~0.3x of take 8; take 12 (size still + front render) → ~0.5x, shipped; take 14 (size still at 0.42 head, no render) → ~0.5x; take 13 (shrink pass on take 8) → unchanged size, zoomed out. Muha Memes/DualFlavor/README.md 'GIFs' section, hf/dogbone_minimax1{1,2,3,4}.txt.

laws.claim: gpt-image-2 edits that put the device into a superhero comic/cartoon frame are refused by the safety system: Batman-slapping-Robin (comic panel) and the 1960s Spider-Man-pointing frame both failed 2/2 with the same prompt shape that passed on Stonks, Waiting Skeleton, Sad Pablo, Sleeping Shaq, the Uno man, the virgin/chad photo pair, the trolley line drawing and Types of Headaches. laws.claim: When a template already carries printed/handwritten text, the prompt must name it and say it stays. Calling the area 'blank' made gpt-image-2 erase the Uno card's 'OR draw 25'; the corrected prompt ('the handwritten OR draw 25 stays exactly as it is; add the words pick a side above it in the same marker handwriting') rendered 2/2 with clean lettering. Short labels in a template's own font (Types of Headaches, Uno) are safe to ask gpt for; long copy still goes through the deterministic card.

taste.reading: For the Dual Flavor the operator wants MAINSTREAM caption-format templates where a character holds the device as the punchline and the caption carries the choice/switch joke. Art memes (public-domain paintings), no-face photo templates and 'device as scenery' (planet, tower, floating between wolves) did not land for this device even though the magnetic art memes had. Celebrity likeness (Drake) was accepted; the woman-cat removal is a joke/format call, not a moderation one.
taste.format: ALL memes ship 4:5 portrait (IG feed). Build the 4:5 canvas deterministically (to45.py: pad with the template's own background colour where it is flat, crop where the content allows, outpaint with gpt-image-2 only for full-bleed scenes) and place captions in fractions of the final canvas.
notes: 'Move the device closer to his hand' = the device must relate to the character's gesture, not float in the template's original prop position.
Remove any artist credit / watermark that rides in the template gutter (Two Buttons: crop panels to their black borders).
taste.round2Verdict: 'a bit corny — think about memes a company meme page would post, not too edgy but something relatable to gen z' (2026-09-10). Diagnosis: the round-2 captions were product-forward ad copy (tagline, mg, 'switch mid-sesh') set in Impact caps on 2012-era templates. A Gen Z brand page posts a lowercase deadpan caption bar over a reaction image, never names the product or the tagline, and lets the device sit in the frame incidentally.

voice.format: 1080x1350: white caption bar on top, Helvetica Neue Medium ~46px black, lowercase sentence case, image full-width below (genz_card.py `bar`); or TikTok-style white bold with a thin dark stroke centred on a 4:5 phone photo (`tiktok`).
voice.copy: relatable situations in first person or 'friend: / me:' — indecision, switching sides, the puff counter as a scoreboard, 2am, the group chat. No brand name, no 'Dual Flavor All-In-One', no mg, no 'switch mid-sesh', no caps, no exclamation marks, no slang stacking.
voice.imagery: reaction images: deadpan cat at the table, unbothered capybara, caught-out hamster, dog balancing the device on its nose, Squidward at the blinds, the monkey puppet; plus phone-photo moods (green LED in a dark bedroom, the nightstand at 2am) and the two LED renders as 'what i say vs what i do'. Never show consumption; the device is held, balanced or lying there.
voice.avoid: art memes, no-face 'concept' images, device-as-scenery, Impact caps, product copy in the caption, celebrities as the joke.
